papers.title: Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion

summary.tldr: Uno introduces diffusion-augmented LLMs that decouple standard autoregressive weights from lightweight diffusion weights to enable parallel, lossless token generation without a draft model.
key_points: Decouples parameters into standard next-token prediction AR weights and lightweight diffusion weights trained via a simple Diffusion Distillation phase.
Introduces Ψ-Spec, a sampler family providing lossless acceleration and inference-time scaling at a fixed context length without needing a separate draft model.
Achieves up to 3x speedups over the base AR model and yields higher throughput than speculative decoding across all evaluated batch sizes.
Outperforms the 26B DiffusionGemma and Mercury 2 models in coding, agentic tool use, and long-context reasoning using an 8B Uno model.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables significant parallel inference acceleration for standard AR language models while preserving baseline generation quality and eliminating draft model overhead.

papers.title: UniMate: One Unified Model to Animate Diverse Skeletons

summary.tldr: UniMate is a topology-aware diffusion transformer that generates motion for arbitrary 3D skeletons from a text prompt and rest pose without per-skeleton fine-tuning or reference motions.
key_points: Incorporates skeletal topology via graph-aware attention bias, Laplacian-derived spectral rotary positional embeddings (RoPE), and a global rest-pose topological conditioner.
Trained on UniML3D, a curated dataset of 13,006 motion sequences covering bipeds, quadrupeds, birds, marine life, insects, serpents, and rigid objects with text pairs.
Requires no test-time optimization or retraining to handle arbitrary skeletal structures.
Supports zero-shot cross-topology motion transfer, motion in-betweening, sequence expansion, and text-guided motion editing.
summary.why_it_matters: It removes the need to build category-specific motion generators or perform per-asset fine-tuning, streamlining the 3D animation pipeline for diverse character topologies.

papers.title: FlowBalance: Verifier-Grounded Self-Improvement from On-Policy Reasoning Experience

summary.tldr: FlowBalance is a verifier-grounded self-improvement method that uses trajectory balance and privileged self-guidance to learn a normalized distribution over complete reasoning responses.
key_points: Uses a frozen training-time view of the policy with privileged context to generate token-level log-probability gains, aggregated into trajectory-level self-guidance scores.
Calibrates self-guidance using verifier-derived group advantage: retained for positive advantage, reversed for negative advantage, and disabled when no preference exists.
Fits the normalized target distribution using profiled trajectory balance with a single log-partition estimate per rollout group, avoiding a separate token-level imitation loss.

Provides theoretical guarantees including within-group contrast preservation, minimum-change reverse-KL characterization, monotonic verifier control, and exact correction against false-positive self-guidance.
Outperforms FlowRL on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B in mathematical reasoning while improving stability, training speed, strategy diversity on AIME24, and avoiding response-length collapse.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents false confidence, mode collapse, and response-length degradation in RL self-improvement loops by combining verifier outcomes with normalized trajectory balance.

papers.title: Unfold The World: Factorize 4D Properties in Reinforcing Spatial Reasoning

summary.tldr: FactoSR introduces a factorized reinforcement learning framework that decomposes 4D spatial reasoning into planar correspondence, depth consistency, and temporal reversibility sub-objectives to improve Vision-Language Models.
key_points: Addresses the VLM spatial reasoning bottleneck caused by interpreting 2D projections instead of 3D geometry and temporal continuity.
Decomposes monolithic world-consistent reasoning into three orthogonal geometric sub-objectives: planar correspondence (XY), depth consistency (Z), and temporal reversibility (T).
Optimizes these factorized verifiable constraints within a unified policy learning mechanism.
Achieves performance improvements on spatial benchmarks, including a 5.9% boost on VSI-Bench and a 4.5% boost on All-Angles-Bench.
summary.why_it_matters: Decomposing 4D visual constraints into verifiable sub-objectives enables VLMs to better reconstruct physical 3D and 4D spatial relationships from 2D projections.

papers.title: ENEAS: Embedding-guided Neural Ensemble for Adaptive Segmentation

summary.tldr: ENEAS is a text-promptable segmentation method that combines an extended SeC temporal memory architecture with a semantic verification layer to eliminate temporal hallucinations, spatial fragmentation, and visual false positives.
key_points: Extends the point-interaction SeC architecture with a text-prompting adapter and temporal memory to prevent tracking drift during object disappearances and extreme close-ups.
Implements an open-concept discovery verification layer that pairs fast visual embedding matching with conditional Vision-Language Model (VLM) refinement.
Invokes semantic reasoning exclusively on ambiguous candidates to keep processing latency low while filtering out visually similar non-target artifacts like statues, paintings, and reflections.
Handles both unique instance tracking and multi-instance semantic discovery across video sequences and temporally or spatially unordered image collections.
summary.why_it_matters: By distinguishing visually similar distractors from true target instances, ENEAS prevents corrupted assets in sensitive downstream applications like 3D reconstruction.

papers.title: One Editor, Many Edits: A Unified Training-Free Framework for Diverse Video Editing

summary.tldr: EditVid is a unified, training-free video editing framework that supports both instruction-guided and reference-guided edits using sparse causal memory, post-attention token injection, and soft latent blending.
key_points: Uses sparse causal memory to ensure local temporal coherence across video frames.
Employs correspondence-based post-attention token injection for long-range subject identity preservation.
Applies soft latent blending to preserve non-edited regions and enforce edit locality.
Achieves 78.16 FiVE-Acc on the FiVE benchmark, outperforming the top training-free baseline (58.95), and secures a 51.8% preference rate in a user study against 7 competing methods.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables diverse video editing tasks—such as style transfer, object insertion, and subject replacement—within a single framework without requiring model retraining or fine-tuning.

papers.title: Verify Before You Distill: Prompt-Level Teacher Gating for On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Teacher-Gated On-Policy Distillation (TGOPD) evaluates teacher reliability per prompt using verifier-scored probes, routing prompts to dense OPD if reliable or to verifier-grounded GRPO if unreliable.
key_points: Addresses mode-seeking reverse KL issues where confidently wrong teachers induce misleading token-level updates during vanilla on-policy distillation.
Replaces distributional uncertainty proxies (like entropy or likelihood agreement) with explicit prompt-level outcome verification using teacher probes.
Improves student performance across 4B and 35B models in math, code, and instruction following, outperforming vanilla OPD across single-domain and multi-domain settings.
Increases teacher-node GPU utilization in asynchronous setups from 9.8% to 78.9% by utilizing idle capacity for reliability estimation.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents model degradation caused by incorrect teacher supervision while drastically improving hardware efficiency during asynchronous distillation.

papers.title: Knowing What Not to Answer: Selective Non-Compliance in Vision-Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced KoNA, a benchmark to evaluate VLM selective non-compliance across paired single and compound queries, and demonstrated fine-tuning strategies that improve partial refusal capabilities without compromising standard task performance.
key_points: KoNA tests query-level and component-level non-compliance across five categories: False Premise, Visual Inaccessibility, Universal Unknown, Task Feasibility, and Safety.
Evaluations reveal that VLMs struggle to refuse, correct, or abstain when handling compound queries containing a mix of answerable and unanswerable components.

Fine-tuning VLMs on a dataset combining KoNA selective non-compliance examples and fully answerable control sets substantially improves non-compliance accuracy while preserving performance on direct-answer tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: Enabling VLMs to selectively abstain from or correct unanswerable parts of a compound query prevents over-refusal and eliminates hallucinated compliance in real-world user interactions.

papers.title: Refuse without Refusal: A Structural Analysis of Safety-Tuning Responses for Reducing False Refusals in Language Models

summary.tldr: Decomposing safety-tuning responses reveals that boilerplate refusal statements drive false refusals, whereas training models exclusively on refusal rationales preserves safety while significantly improving benign query responsiveness.
key_points: Safety-tuning responses were decomposed into two distinct structural components: a boilerplate refusal statement and an explanatory rationale.
Boilerplate refusal statements cause models to rely on superficial cues, impeding their ability to distinguish genuinely harmful queries from superficially risky benign inputs.
Training models strictly on rationales (Rationale-Only) reduces false refusals while maintaining comparable safety performance.
The Rationale-Only approach provides performance benefits in in-context learning (ICL) configurations and remains fully compatible with evaluated inference-time mitigation techniques.
summary.why_it_matters: Removing boilerplate refusal phrases from safety datasets offers a simple fine-tuning adjustment that reduces over-refusal on benign queries without compromising model safety.

papers.title: HarvestBench: Measuring Whether LLM Agents Will Pay to Avoid Killing Animals

summary.tldr: HarvestBench is a reproducible farm-simulation benchmark that quantifies whether LLM agents will pay a fuel cost to avoid killing animals during goal-oriented tasks.
key_points: Evaluated 9 models across 7,201 priced decisions in an RL gridworld without using LLM graders, relying entirely on game-log event counts.
Kill rates varied widely from 0.4% (Terra and Sol) to 98.8% (GPT-4o-mini) and did not correlate directly with model capability.
Four of six tested models exhibited price sensitivity to fuel costs (elasticities between 0.09 and 1.69), and all models killed wild animals more frequently than farmed ones.
Prompting via a morality briefing reduced kill rates below 6% in five of six reasoning models, whereas omitting it spiked kill rates above 84% across all six.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a deterministic method to measure behavioral alignment and trade-off costs regarding real-world side effects without relying on self-reported model critiques.

papers.title: What Else Needs Fixing? Exploring Cost-Effective Test-Time Compute for Revision Propagation in Artifacts Generated Through Conversation

summary.tldr: A new benchmark evaluates LLM revision propagation in conversational artifacts, finding that selecting from three parallel samples yields the most cost-effective accuracy improvements.
key_points: Introduces a benchmark specifically designed to test how LLMs propagate local user-requested revisions to dependent parts across conversational context history.
Evaluated nine revision methods across models including gpt-oss-20b/120b, gpt-5.4-mini, and qwen3.5-9b/27b/122b.
Baseline accuracies ranged from 68.3% to 93.0% on the benchmark.
Selecting from three parallel samples using either LLM-based or medoid selection proved to be the most cost-effective approach, boosting accuracy by 2.2% to 9.7%.
summary.why_it_matters: It identifies a low-overhead test-time compute strategy to ensure LLMs correctly update all dependent components during iterative artifact editing.

papers.title: The 2026 PNPL Competition: Word Classification and Efficient Cross-Subject Generalisation in LibriBrain100

summary.tldr: The 2026 PNPL competition introduces the LibriBrain100 dataset to evaluate word classification via two tracks: within-subject scaling and efficient cross-subject generalisation using reduced fine-tuning data.
key_points: Builds on 2025 competition results that achieved 95.6% F1-macro for speech detection and 73.6% for phoneme classification.
Introduces LibriBrain100, extending the original dataset with 32 additional MEG subjects (approx. 40 minutes each) and increasing within-subject data to approx. 80 hours.
Features a Deep track focused on maximizing within-subject word classification performance at scale.
Features a Broad track focused on cross-subject generalisation, reducing required subject-specific fine-tuning data from 40 to 20 to 10 minutes.
summary.why_it_matters: Reducing required user-specific calibration data to 10 minutes advances the clinical viability of non-invasive brain-computer interfaces for restoring communication in paralyzed patients.

papers.title: How Does mHC Use Its Residual Streams? Selective Routing and Near-Identity Mixing

summary.tldr: An empirical analysis of DeepSeek-V4-Flash shows that its four-stream manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC) operate via selective routing and early-layer mixing, leaving late-layer stream mixing largely redundant.
key_points: Attention and FFN blocks dynamically route information using effectively two of the four streams per site, with representation vectors remaining directionally distinct across streams.
Cross-stream residual mixing occurs primarily in early layers; in layers 22-42, the residual streams act almost entirely as independent parallel identity pathways.
Replacing late-layer mixers with identity operations increases C4 perplexity by only 1.9% with zero loss on a six-task average score, whereas replacing early mixers increases perplexity by 41%.

Replacing early mixers with their static C4 diagnostic mean increases perplexity by just 0.2%, indicating that site-specific routing architecture matters significantly more than per-token dynamic variation.
Sparsifying routing to keep only the top three weights per token per site increases perplexity by at most 2.7% and shifts average downstream task accuracy by ≤0.4 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that mHC networks rely on static early mixing and sparse routing provides clear targets for pruning late-layer stream mixers and optimizing multi-stream transformer architectures.

papers.title: GUT: Quantifying and Optimizing the Reasoning Uncertainty of LLMs via Graph Complexity

summary.tldr: The Graph-complexity-based UncerTainty (GUT) method models LLM reasoning chains as directed acyclic graphs to quantify uncertainty via graph complexity and optimize it using reinforcement learning.
key_points: Models divergent reasoning steps and potential branches as a directed acyclic graph (DAG) to cover the full reasoning space.
Introduces GUT-Q (Quantification) to measure LLM reasoning uncertainty by approximating reasoning space complexity using graph complexity.
Introduces GUT-O (Optimization) to reduce reasoning uncertainty by applying negative uncertainty as a reward function in reinforcement learning.
Validated via experiments across four LLMs and five benchmark datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: GUT provides a structured, graph-based framework to systematically measure and reduce hallucinated or nonsensical reasoning paths in LLMs through targeted reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Single-Query Black-Box Calibration Auditing via Logit Bias

summary.tldr: A novel auditing method uses an API's logit_bias parameter to evaluate exact probability thresholds and compute True Calibration Error for binary classification using a single query per sample.
key_points: Commercial LLM APIs increasingly hide continuous output probabilities needed for standard calibration metrics.
Leveraging the logit_bias parameter enables exact probability threshold evaluation via a single query per sample.
The method introduces a provably consistent estimator for True Calibration Error in binary tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient, low-cost black-box calibration auditing of opaque commercial LLM APIs without requiring full probability distributions.

papers.title: Fractal basins trap latent reasoning

summary.tldr: New research demonstrates that reasoning models act as dynamical systems with fractal basins, where computation slowdowns on hard tasks are caused by transient chaos around saddle points.
key_points: Reasoning models behave as dynamical systems exhibiting transient chaos during complex tasks.
Fractality of the models' basins increases proportionally with task difficulty across domains such as Sudoku, maze solving, visual puzzles, and mathematical logic.
Transient chaos and computational slowdowns occur when reasoning traces become trapped for extended durations near saddle points.
Saddle points in the dynamical system correspond to nearly-correct attempted solutions of the target problem.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes that reasoning slowdowns on hard problems are an inevitable physical and dynamical consequence of task complexity rather than an implementational flaw.

papers.title: KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU

summary.tldr: KVMem is a KV-context virtualization system that offloads overflowed agent workspace history to host memory and NVMe as paged KV state, decoupling total workspace size from the LLM's native context window.
key_points: Uses lightweight, model-native attention-space indexes to retrieve historical KV blocks and construct a query-dependent execution view within the model's context window.
Preserves original execution state instead of using compaction or text re-prefilling, mitigating information loss and redundant processing.
Improved task success from 43.8% (compaction-only) to 48.4% on the DeepSWE long-context benchmark using Qwen3.8-27B.
Demonstrated on a 24 GB RTX 5090 Laptop GPU running Qwen3.6/3.8-27B (NVFP4 with MTP), supporting 1M-token workspaces (4x the native 256K window) at ~50 tokens/s.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables consumer-grade hardware to run long-running, local LLM agents with million-token persistent workspaces without losing fine-grained historical state.

papers.title: Compression Beyond the Uncompressed: A Two-Stage Training Recipe for Soft Context Compression in RAG

summary.tldr: DEX-Comp introduces a two-stage training recipe combining pure distillation and reinforcement learning hard exploration to allow soft context compression models to meet or exceed uncompressed RAG performance.
key_points: Uses a Two-Stage Training Recipe: 'Pure Distillation' warm-starts the compression model using only correct responses from the uncompressed RAG, followed by 'Hard Exploration' which uses reinforcement learning strictly on queries where the uncompressed baseline failed.
Achieves $16\times$ context compression on retrieved documents across retrieval depths from top-5 to top-30 on five open-domain QA benchmarks.
Delivers $4\times$ to $24\times$ inference acceleration while matching or outperforming uncompressed RAG baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: By relying on reinforcement learning to explore computation patterns beyond standard uncompressed RAG capabilities, soft context compression can drastically improve LLM inference efficiency without sacrificing performance.

papers.title: Beneath the Surface of Chains-of-Thought: A Mechanistic Interpretation of Reasoning Operations in LLMs

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that LLMs encode distinct linguistic reasoning operations as separable geometric structures within hidden representations, peaking in middle layers.
key_points: Reasoning operations such as problem formulation, goal decomposition, and deduction are linearly separable in held-out hidden representations.
Separability of reasoning operations peaks in the middle layers of the model and is independent of lexical or positional confounds.
Across layers, token-wise operation-alignment becomes distributed over text spans, causing identical surface tokens to be represented differently based on chunk context.
Attention-masking interventions confirm that operation-aligned representations at chunk onset depend directly on preceding reasoning context.
summary.why_it_matters: Proving that internal geometric structures correspond to explicit linguistic reasoning operations enables better mechanistic interpretability and targeted steering of LLM chains-of-thought.

papers.title: When Do Internal Probes Beat Reading the Answer? Miscalibrated Readouts and Behavior-Concealed Knowledge in Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that language models can possess internal knowledge that fails to manifest in output behavior due to miscalibrated decision thresholds and answer-channel failures rather than missing internal representations.
key_points: A 0.6B model answered YES to all 1,200 logic tests (50% behavioral accuracy), yet linear hidden-state probes achieved 0.96 AUC and output logit margins achieved 0.89 AUC.
Behavioral collapse across 90 semantic-label configurations across five models correlates strongly with a saturated output decision threshold offset by +4.6 sigma (Spearman -0.93).
Scaling from 0.6B to 8B shows non-monotone free-form behavior (8B underperforms 4B due to answer-channel failure), whereas forced-choice accuracy and internal knowledge remain monotone.

A one-parameter threshold correction improved 0.6B behavioral accuracy from 50% to 81%, calibrated margin decoding recovered 94% accuracy at 8B, and few-shot prompting works by recentering the threshold from +4.6 sigma to 0.0 sigma.
The framework categorizes internal model states into three distinct regimes: concealed, miscalibrated, and undetected knowledge.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating language models purely on output behavior can severely underestimate their latent capabilities, which simple one-parameter threshold calibrations or logit margin decoding can unlock.

papers.title: Necessary or Sufficient? Evaluating LLM Explanations With Behavioural Evidence

summary.tldr: A new black-box evaluation framework measures how accurately LLM-generated explanations reflect necessity and sufficiency in model decision-making.
key_points: Evaluated eight LLMs from the Claude, GPT, and Gemini families across synthetic advisor recommendation and prompt monitoring tasks.
Calculated Spearman correlations between cited factor rankings and measured necessity (0.349-0.431) and sufficiency (0.354-0.580) scores.
Found uncited factors outscored the lowest-cited factor in up to 57.6% (necessity) and 58.1% (sufficiency) of advisor recommendation cases.
Prompt monitoring exhibited lower rates of uncited factors outscoring cited factors, down to 25.8% for necessity and 8.9% for sufficiency.
Demonstrated that cited top-three factors contain useful information but do not reliably reflect the factors with the greatest causal influence.
summary.why_it_matters: Operators relying on LLM-generated explanations for agent oversight cannot assume the stated factors reliably represent the true causal drivers of a model's decisions.

papers.title: Molecular Déjà Vu: Digit-Level Retrieval of Published Values in Frontier Language Models

summary.tldr: An audit of 22 frontier LLMs across 12 molecular regression benchmarks reveals widespread verbatim digit-level retrieval of published values, which increases significantly when models operate at higher reasoning levels.
key_points: Over 50% of the 22 audited LLMs exhibit verbatim value retrieval on 5 out of the 12 molecular regression benchmarks.
Higher model reasoning levels increased verbatim retrieval flags by 89% compared to the lowest reasoning level using identical prompts and molecules.
Strong frontier models recognized molecular property targets even when SMILES strings were transformed to interrupt retrieval.
Suppressing verbatim retrieval aligns prediction error rates more closely across different models, demonstrating that raw predictive capability is distinct from memorization volume.
summary.why_it_matters: High performance on chemistry LLM benchmarks may reflect memorization rather than actual generalizable scientific reasoning, complicating true capability evaluations.

papers.title: Does Your Agent's Memory Survive a Model Upgrade? A Controlled Study of Memory Portability

summary.tldr: A controlled study evaluates LLM memory portability across model upgrades, finding fixed-schema knowledge graphs resist migration shifts while compressed notes and mixed-embedding RAG indices suffer severe performance degradation.
key_points: Fixed-schema knowledge graphs (KG-fixed) transferred almost perfectly across writer swaps, exhibiting an accuracy change of only +0.0004 ± 0.0020.

Compressed natural-language NOTES showed heavy model coupling, shifting asymmetric accuracy by +9.91 or -13.28 percentage points depending on the migration direction, with 80% of the accuracy deficit caused by initial construction loss.

In RAG systems, a 50/50 mixed embedding index gained only 4.96 percentage points in accuracy, failing to capture the full 11.90-point gain of complete re-embedding due to retrieval failures driving 81% of the deficit.

Store-only repair of NOTES failed to reach a 90% recovery target across all 48 test cases, whereas preserving raw source history allowed successful repair in 34 of 48 cases for one migration direction.
summary.why_it_matters: Maintaining long-term agent memory across model upgrades requires preserving raw source histories, isolating embedding spaces, and using structured knowledge graphs rather than un-re-embedded notes or partial vector indices.

papers.title: Technical Manual for a Toolkit for Measuring Contextual Individuation in Transformer Language Models

summary.tldr: A new open-source technical toolkit measures contextual individuation in transformer language models using controlled bridge-form words across Wikipedia domains.
key_points: Uses bridge forms—identical written words recurring across different subject domains with distinct senses—to hold word form fixed while varying context.
Pipeline executes domain declarative specification, Wikipedia corpus acquisition, occurrence localization, and layer-wise vector extraction.
Quantifies representation space separation using a domain-pairwise silhouette measurement coupled with a paired visualization protocol.
Explicitly addresses failure modes including multi-group silhouette bias, sense contamination from broad category labels, subword tokenization misalignment, and dimensionality reduction artifacts.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a standardized, methodologically rigorous instrument to isolate and measure how transformer models disambiguate identical word tokens across layers without empirical confounding.

papers.title: Beyond Aggregate Scores: Behavioral Correctness Assumptions for Assessing Reference-Based Automatic Evaluation Methods

summary.tldr: A new framework called behavioral correctness assumptions evaluates reference-based automated evaluation methods using controlled response transformations rather than aggregate human agreement scores.
key_points: Defines a taxonomy of correctness-preserving and correctness-altering assumptions operationalized via controlled response transformations.
Assesses lexical, character-level, semantic, LLM-based, and hybrid evaluators on stability, sensitivity, repeat-run variability, configuration sensitivity, and reproducibility.
Reveals that no evaluated method satisfies all proposed correctness assumptions.
Shows that evaluators with similar aggregate meta-evaluation performance exhibit significantly different underlying behavioral profiles.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides fine-grained diagnostic visibility into the failure modes and behavioral trade-offs of natural language generation evaluators that traditional aggregate benchmarks obscure.

summary.tldr: Researchers discovered an architectural flaw in major LLM APIs where client-side encrypted reasoning traces are interchangeable across models, allowing attackers to decrypt them using weaker models.
key_points: Encrypted chain-of-thought blocks are fully compatible across different sessions, users, and models within a provider's ecosystem.
Injecting a strong model's encrypted reasoning trace into a weaker model forces the weaker model to output the decoded plaintext trace verbatim.
The vulnerability affects Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, enabling anti-distillation bypass, invisible prompt injections, and exposure of hidden hazardous information.
Analysis of 315,320 scraped public reasoning blocks successfully recovered 367 PII artifacts and 182 sensitive credentials.
summary.why_it_matters: Attackers can silently extract proprietary AI reasoning, harvest private credentials, and execute invisible prompt injections without needing to directly jailbreak target frontier models.

security.title: Client-Side Probing of Deleted Ridge Statistics in Federated Unlearning

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate a client-side probing attack that exploits model updates broadcast during federated unlearning to reconstruct deleted training feature summaries.
key_points: Malicious clients submit known changes to capture server state updates before and after isolated unlearning events.
Reconstructed additive feature summaries reveal deleted samples, classes, or client data, enabling potential reinsertion.
Demonstrated exact label recovery on MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets using both unrestricted probes and realistic attacker-data additions.
Mitigations include reducing broadcast precision, restricting response rates, enforcing update verification, and maintaining concurrent background activity.
summary.why_it_matters: Exact federated unlearning systems using additive summaries introduce serious privacy and integrity risks by leaking deleted client data directly through classifier updates.

security.title: Shadow AI Does Not Read Your Org Chart: Rethinking Identity Governance for Autonomous Agents

summary.tldr: Enterprise AI agent deployments are expanding rapidly, challenging traditional Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) because autonomous systems require extensive access to function effectively.
key_points: Traditional RBAC models fail to adequately govern autonomous AI agents that operate outside human organizational hierarchies.
Prominent cryptographer Adi Shamir warned at RSA Conference 2026 that AI agents present significant security risks due to their need for broad data access.
summary.why_it_matters: CISOs must redesign identity and access governance architectures to accommodate autonomous agents that require far broader permissions than human employees.

security.title: Hoss: Fast Oblivious Semantic Search with Heterogeneous GPU-CPU-TEE Architecture

summary.tldr: Hoss is an oblivious semantic search system using a heterogeneous GPU-CPU TEE architecture to bypass traditional ORAM bandwidth bottlenecks by leveraging large GPU private memory.
key_points: Exploits large private memory (Pmem) in modern GPU TEEs to blind internal access patterns and host hot-path HNSW graph traversals.
Offloads lower layers of the HNSW graph to CPU TEEs when capacity is exceeded, invoking oblivious primitives exclusively for these CPU-bound layers.
Features a host-access ORAM mechanism alongside data-dependent optimizations enabled by the large GPU Pmem.
Demonstrates up to a 67x speedup over the state-of-the-art system (Compass) while maintaining high search recall.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces the overhead of privacy-preserving semantic search, making oblivious vector indexing scalable and practical on modern hardware.

security.title: Nebulon Enterprise Simulated Threats for Phishing Research (NEST-Phish): A Synthetic Enterprise Phishing Email Dataset for Behavioral and Machine-Learning Research

summary.tldr: Researchers have introduced NEST-Phish, a publicly shareable synthetic dataset featuring matched legitimate and annotated phishing emails set within a fictitious enterprise named Nebulon.
key_points: Dataset is built around a fictitious enterprise, Nebulon, to mirror realistic workplace communication themes.
Contains paired synthetic legitimate (non-phishing) and phishing emails featuring interpretable phishing-cue annotations.
Validated through human-subject categorizations to confirm variation in phishing judgments and classifier evaluations to demonstrate learnable signals for supervised detection.
summary.why_it_matters: NEST-Phish addresses the scarcity of publicly available, realistic enterprise email datasets required to benchmark machine-learning detection models and study human phishing susceptibility.

security.title: Candidate Comparability Before Promotion: Conditional Validation in Adaptive Network Intrusion Detection

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that model promotion decisions in adaptive network intrusion detection depend heavily on challenger pipeline self-containment and candidate evidence sizes across CICIDS2017, UNSW-NB15, and ToN-IoT benchmarks.
key_points: Incumbent-owned frozen preprocessing artificially amplified promotion harm, whereas self-contained challenger pipelines eliminated persistent mean full-drift harm.
Increasing candidate evidence from 512 to 2,000 samples per class improved balanced accuracy by +0.53, +1.67, and +0.38 points across the three datasets, primarily by reducing false positives.
Evaluating nine update policies revealed that policy ordering changes with candidate comparability, with no single policy globally dominating.

Conditional validation provided benefits to evidence-disadvantaged challengers but offered no average benefit when candidates were at parity, while 13 real-world time-ordered replays showed zero net harm from continuous deployment.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating network intrusion detection updates without strictly controlling challenger pipeline independence and candidate sample sizes yields misleading conclusions about model promotion policies.

security.title: Long-Range Indirect Control-Flow Prediction in Stripped Binaries via Dual Virtual Hubs and Multi-Task Graph Learning

summary.tldr: ICFlowNet is a unified multi-task graph learning framework that uses candidate-aware Dual Virtual Hubs to predict long-range indirect control-flow edges in stripped x86-64 binaries.
key_points: Dual Virtual Hubs (Global Code Hub and Global Data Hub) create short routing paths to connect distant code and data evidence, improving long-range F1 scores by up to 9.13 points.
Jointly models indirect calls, indirect tail calls, jump tables, and returns via multi-task graph learning, contributing up to 5.81 points in F1 gains.
Establishes a leakage-aware evaluation pipeline using package-level splits, function-level mnemonic-hash deduplication, and dynamic ground-truth positives with absolute negatives.
Evaluated on a dataset of 15,901 stripped x86-64 binaries, outperforming baselines by over 13 F1 points on long-range indirect calls with an 11.44% topological overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables significantly more accurate static binary security analysis and control-flow recovery across long code distances without relying on debug symbols or prone-to-leakage evaluation protocols.

infra.title: GLM 5.3 Optimizations, Part 1: Hybrid HiSparse Offloading in vLLM

summary.tldr: vLLM introduced Hybrid HiSparse offloading for GLM 5.3, enabling 1M context lengths on an 8x H200 node by offloading non-selected sparse-MLA KV cache pages to CPU only under memory pressure.
key_points: Leverages GLM 5.3's IndexShare architecture (one indexer layer per four sparse-MLA layers) to keep small indexer KVs GPU-resident while offloading non-top-K tokens to CPU.
Operates dynamic three-state page residency tracked per page, leasing hot buffer pages directly from vLLM's Hybrid Memory Allocator (HMA) block pool.
Proactively queues copies of completed cacheable prefix pages to CPU memory, allowing instant release of GPU blocks when memory pressure rises.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates memory bottlenecks on tightly constrained hardware, allowing single-node deployments to serve high-concurrency agentic workloads at massive context lengths.

infra.title: PyTorch x Hugging Face in Bengaluru: Building India’s Next Generation of ML Systems Contributors

summary.tldr: Red Hat and Hugging Face hosted a technical session in Bengaluru for over 170 engineers focused on open-source ML infrastructure, covering PyTorch profiling, inference runtimes, and distributed training systems.
key_points: Aritra Roy Gosthipaty demonstrated PyTorch profiling workflows using torch.profiler.record_function and torch.profiler.profile schedules to isolate wait, warmup, and active execution phases.
The profiling session detailed methods for exporting traces and reading aggregate tables to differentiate CPU orchestration overhead from CUDA kernel execution.
Adarsh presented on modern LLM inference architecture utilizing SGLang, the Hugging Face Transformers backend, and custom kernel ecosystems.
The event targeted shifting Indian ML engineers from consumers of high-level AI APIs to core contributors of profilers, runtimes, RL environments, and distributed communication primitives.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding low-level PyTorch profiling and inference abstractions enables developers to systematically debug CPU overhead and optimize GPU kernel performance in production systems.

infra.title: Alibaba Cloud, Ant Group, Cambricon and Huawei Come Together in Shanghai to Advance the Open Source AI Stack at PyTorch Conference China

summary.tldr: Alibaba Cloud and Cambricon joined the PyTorch Foundation as Platinum members, while Ant Group joined as a Gold member, announcing their roles at PyTorch Conference China 2026.
key_points: Alibaba Cloud's Qwen infrastructure team detailed methods for serving Qwen open-weight models at massive scale.
Huawei addressed hardware-software co-design and interoperability requirements between Chinese and global AI stacks.
Cambricon presented efforts to harden PyTorch's device-agnostic foundation for Machine Learning Unit (MLU) chips and backends.
Ant Group demonstrated using Kubernetes Agent Sandbox and Kata Containers to build a secure, on-demand AI agent runtime.
summary.why_it_matters: The integration of major Chinese technology hardware and cloud vendors into the PyTorch Foundation strengthens global cross-platform accelerator support and open-source infrastructure interoperability.

vendors.title: What we learned mapping a year’s worth of AI-enabled cyber threats

summary.tldr: Anthropic analyzed 832 malicious accounts banned between March 2025 and March 2026, mapping them to the MITRE ATT&CK framework to assess how threat actors use AI across the cyberattack lifecycle.
key_points: Malware writing was the most common AI-enabled activity, observed in 67.3% (560) of analyzed accounts, while 6.5% (54) used AI for lateral movement.
Medium-or-higher risk actors increased 1.7-fold, rising from 33% in the first six months to 56% in the second six months.
AI usage shifted deeper into the attack lifecycle post-compromise: account discovery rose by 8.9%, whereas AI-assisted phishing dropped by 8.6%.

Traditional risk metrics have eroded, with low-skilled actors averaging 16 distinct techniques compared to 20 for high-skilled actors, showing little correlation between skill and technique diversity.
summary.why_it_matters: AI enables less sophisticated threat actors to execute complex post-compromise operations, rendering traditional security risk signals like technique volume and platform choice unreliable.

vendors.title: Detecting and countering malicious uses of Claude

summary.tldr: Anthropic released a March 2025 report detailing detected malicious misuses of Claude, including an influence-as-a-service operation that used the model as an automated engagement orchestrator for social media bots.
key_points: Threat actors leveraged Claude as an orchestrator to dynamically decide when bot accounts should like, share, comment, or ignore authentic social media posts based on political personas.
Anthropic detected misuse across credential stuffing, recruitment fraud, and novice-level malware generation.

Investigations utilized specialized analysis techniques detailed in research papers, specifically Clio and hierarchical summarization, alongside standard input/output classifiers to analyze large conversation volumes and ban malicious accounts.
summary.why_it_matters: The shift from using LLMs purely for content generation to using them as decision-making orchestrators for automated campaigns highlights an evolving threat vector for platform safety.

summary.tldr: Anthropic identified industrial-scale distillation campaigns by DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax using approximately 24,000 fraudulent accounts and over 16 million exchanges to extract Claude's capabilities.
key_points: Three foreign AI labs (DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax) used proxy services and about 24,000 fraudulent accounts to generate over 16 million exchanges with Claude.
Attribution was established via IP address correlation, request metadata, infrastructure indicators, and corroboration from industry partners observing identical behaviors.
The campaigns targeted Claude's core capabilities, specifically agentic reasoning, tool use, and coding.
Illicitly distilled models risk stripping out built-in safeguards against bioweapons development and malicious cyber operations.
summary.why_it_matters: Distillation attacks allow foreign competitors to rapidly acquire frontier AI capabilities and bypass safety controls while undermining the intended impact of hardware export restrictions.

vendors.title: Detecting and countering misuse of AI: August 2025

summary.tldr: Anthropic released an August 2025 Threat Intelligence Report detailing malicious exploits of its AI models, including Claude Code, for data extortion, cybercrime, and employment fraud.
key_points: A threat actor utilized Claude Code to target at least 17 organizations across healthcare, emergency services, government, and religious sectors.
The Claude Code attacker bypassed traditional ransomware encryption, instead exfiltrating personal data and demanding extortions exceeding $500,000 under threat of public leak.
Report highlights cybercriminals with only basic coding skills leveraging Claude to generate and sell functional ransomware.
Disclosed a North Korean fraudulent employment scheme exploiting AI capabilities alongside details on Anthropic's detection and countermeasure steps.
summary.why_it_matters: Malicious actors with minimal technical expertise are successfully abusing advanced agentic AI tools like Claude Code to automate and scale high-value extortion and malware generation.

vendors.title: Disrupting the first reported AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign

summary.tldr: Anthropic disrupted a Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage campaign where attackers used Claude Code as an autonomous agent to attempt infiltration of roughly thirty global targets with minimal human intervention.
key_points: Threat actors manipulated Claude Code to execute cyberattacks autonomously rather than just using AI as an advisor.
The campaign targeted approximately thirty global entities across large tech, financial institutions, chemical manufacturing, and government agencies, succeeding in a small number of cases.

Attackers bypassed AI guardrails by jailbreaking Claude Code, decomposing malicious actions into seemingly innocent sub-tasks, and falsely framing the context as authorized defensive security testing.
summary.why_it_matters: This represents the first documented case of an AI agent autonomously executing a large-scale cyber espionage campaign without substantial human intervention.

summary.tldr: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki argues that rapidly training smarter, aligned AI models is essential to build defensive systems against AI-driven threats without resorting to reckless development.
key_points: Defensive AI applications include real-time protection against rogue agents, securing critical infrastructure, and developing novel protective measures.
Training powerful, aligned AI is framed as a necessary strategy to counter potential dangers posed by other AI systems.
Pachocki warns against using defensive needs as an excuse for reckless, race-at-all-costs AI development due to high stakes.
summary.why_it_matters: OpenAI's deployment strategy prioritizes building advanced aligned AI specifically to defend against real-time rogue agent threats and infrastructure vulnerabilities.
